caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular woven textile pattern with a predominance of blue, white, and orange colors. The textile is composed of several vertical bands that each contain distinct repeating geometric designs. From left to right, the first band features a diamond and cross motif made up of small blue squares interspersed with red-orange accents and white lines, forming a grid-like structure. The next vertical band alternates clusters of white rectangular shapes arranged in a checkerboard pattern on a blue background. The central section features a repeated horizontal motif of orange elongated diamond shapes, surrounded by blue and white, forming a horizontal stripe pattern. To the right, a band mirrors the left-most motifs but with a denser arrangement of the geometric shapes and again uses blue as the background color with orange and white patterns. The far-right band repeats the checkerboard pattern found earlier. The entire textile is presented on a plain, off-white background, and there are no other objects or elements within the image. A small circular stamp with writing and some numbers are present at the bottom right corner of the background.
title: Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
